summary.oneLiner: FY26 was an explicitly self-described year of "transition, correction and strengthening" — Moneyboxx sacrificed growth to fix a book that got caught in the MFI-guardrail spillover, and the asset-quality repair is now visible and large: GNPA 6.61% → 3.59%, NNPA 3.42% → 1.75%, bucket-1/bucket-2 resolution rates at "the highest level achieved by the company since inception". The cost of that repair is that the P&L is barely above breakeven (FY26 PAT ₹1.34cr on ₹232cr total income) because opex (12.8%) is carried against a shrunken ₹893cr AUM. The FY27 thesis is entirely an operating-leverage bet: management has told its lenders a **43–44% AUM jump** and expects credit cost **below 2%**, to be delivered through a secured mix pivot (68% → target ~80% by Mar-27), FLDG/second-loss-backed partnership sourcing that carries no sales cost, and a new solar/renewable-asset product targeted at ~10% of AUM.

order book & pipeline:
Not applicable in the conventional sense (lending business). Pipeline visibility on this call came from three channel signals rather than a book:
- **Solar/renewable ramp (stated monthly progression):** *"in April, we started renewable energy loans and the expansion was around INR50 lakhs, which is 10x in May, and the number could reach about INR5 crores in May."*
- **OEM partnership pipeline:** *"we have been doing OEM partnerships directly. Solar is one example. We are directly dealing with the OEMs to generate business. And in June, another 2 partnerships are starting."*
- **Cattle-loan partnership:** *"on the cattle loan side also, we are joining a partnership with one of the very large unit where we will fund some loans based on the FLDG programs."* Counterparty not named, size not disclosed.

segment / subsidiary detail:
No subsidiaries were discussed — this is a standalone NBFC. Segment detail is by product:
- **Secured MSME business loans (core, ~68% of AUM incl. 5% guarantee-backed unsecured):** ATS ₹6 lakh, run-rate ticket ₹8–9 lakh. **In April the company discontinued sub-₹5-lakh secured tickets for most branches** — *"in April, we discontinued below INR5 lakh ticket size in secured for most of the branches."*
- **Unsecured micro-enterprise loans (run-off):** *"on a branch level, there is only one state which is allowed to do unsecured loan."*
- **Renewable-energy / solar-asset loans (new in FY26):** financing the **replacement of diesel engines** in *"solar atta chakki, oil expellers, jaggery units, telecom towers."* Customer profile: operators with agri land plus a machine business (atta chakki, oil expeller, RO water plant, sheet-metal fabrication). **ATS ~₹4 lakh; tenure ~4 years; interest rate ~22%, overall yield 22.5% rising to ~23–24% including all fees.** Classified as **secured** — *"there is a hypothecation of solar assets against these loans"* — and carries a second-loss guarantee after 3% loss. Critically, *"we are not incurring sales cost here. So these are direct leads which are coming through partners."*
- **Digital lending (launching Q1FY27):** *"This is the quarter we are wanting to start it. It will be a small piece… this will be unsecured lending, just to mention. We will start small here but slowly increase it."* Enabled by the newly released in-house LOS.
- **Credit-protection overlays:** Rabo Foundation — **3.3% first-loss default guarantee**. Shell Foundation — **10% second-loss guarantee after initial 3% loss coverage**, for loans financing green assets.
growth verticals / optionality:
1. **Partnership/OEM-sourced lending with embedded credit protection** — the structural bet of the year. It attacks both cost lines at once: no sales team (opex) and FLDG/second-loss cover (credit cost). Targeted at 20–25% of monthly business.
2. **MSME solarization** — management frames this as demand-pull, not product-push: *"diesel prices have increased and more and more people want to switch to solar power for running atta chakki, oil expellers."* It also doubles as a **seasonality hedge** (see §12).
3. **Branch vintage maturation** — *"Many of our branches are still in early vintage state, particularly within the first 24 months of operation. As these branches mature, productivity continues to improve steadily, and this embedded growth opportunity is expected to support operating leverage and business growth over the coming years without requiring aggressive branch expansion."*
4. **Co-lending in the secured space** — *"We will look for some co-lending partners in the secured space."* Early-stage intent only.
5. **Digital lending** — optionality, explicitly small at launch.
6a. moat & competitive position:
Management evidenced three durable advantages on this call (each with its supporting quote/number):
- **Impact-capital relationships that convert into hard credit enhancement.** The Rabo Foundation **3.3% FLDG** and Shell Foundation **10% second-loss guarantee after initial 3% loss coverage** are not soft ESG affiliations — they are balance-sheet loss absorbers that competitors of this size generally do not carry. Sourced via the Cattle AI platform and para-vet services: *"Different initiatives such as our Cattle AI platform and complementary Para-vet services are also helping us build strong global partnerships with institutions such as Rabo Foundation, Gates Foundation, Water.org, Shell Foundation and Accion."*
- **Proprietary underwriting/collection tech stack for a segment that is normally paper-based** — in-house LOS "Moneyboxx One", the Sikka app, ML/AI-enabled **Cattle AI** underwriting, and **MB Collect** digital collections: *"helping improve underwriting quality, strengthen fraud checks and maintain strong credit discipline."*
- **Senior talent density well above the book's size** — *"my state heads who are managing about INR100 crores here have been managing almost INR2,000 crores from where they have come in… we have taken the best of profiles from the best of the companies who have like 15 to 20 years kind of experience in building this kind of book."* Note this is presented as a **moat and a cost problem simultaneously** — it is the direct cause of the opex overhang in §7.
margins & cost dynamics:
- **The central tension of the story: yield is guided down while opex must come down faster.** Management concedes the yield give-up outright — *"I don't disagree that yield will decrease because of the secured lending or even on the partnership business side"* — and pins the offset on cost: *"But what we are trying to do here is that we have to reduce our opex."*
- **Opex is a denominator problem, not a wage problem** — management's explicit diagnosis: *"Our cost is high. So one of the biggest reasons is that our AUM is low… as AUM grows, the cost will keep coming down… what we have to really work hard on is to improve the AUM, so that the opex automatically starts declining."* And: *"I will not say that as a company we are overpaying or we are bringing staff at a much higher scale. So that is not true. I mean, our costing is aligned with the market."*
- ⚠️ The analyst's framing — *"our employee cost as a percentage of total assets under management also appears on the higher side, basically, if I'm not wrong, it's around 37%, 38%. I don't have the number in front of me right away"* — was **explicitly caveated by the analyst himself** and **never confirmed numerically by management**. Do not propagate it as a company figure.
- **Three-lever cost plan:** (a) partnership sourcing removes sales cost; (b) FLDG/second-loss programs cap credit cost; (c) decentralized credit underwriting cuts turnaround time — *"the deployment of a decentralized credit underwriting model is helping reduce turnaround time and enhance operating efficiency."*
- **Management's own benchmark for what "solved" looks like:** *"even players who work at 15% or 12%, they make money. So it's a lot about getting your credit cost, opex and collection costs under control."*
- FY26 stated levels: **NIM 13.9%, opex 12.8%, credit cost 3.32%** — i.e. on management's own stated numbers the three lines very nearly consume each other, which is consistent with the ₹1.34cr PAT.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
Asset-light lending model — no physical capex programme. The expansion story this quarter is **negative by design**, which is unusual enough to flag:
- **Branch network is shrinking, deliberately:** *"as a conscious strategy, we are not looking to increase our branch network as well… as a branch network, I don't think so we are looking to increase. In fact, it is only coming down. We are consolidating that piece."*
- **Geographic mix-shift rural → Tier 1**, not expansion: *"wherever we feel some of the branches have now fallen into a deep rural kind of a geography, we are trying to kind of convert those branches and then open up branches in Tier 1. Let's say, for example, we opened up 2 new branches in Bangalore -- peripheries of Bangalore… We opened a branch in Jaipur, but kind of slowed down businesses in some of the branches which are more rural and kind of merged those with some of the existing branches in the vicinity."*
- **No new states in FY27:** *"no new states we are opening up in this financial year"* — footprint stays at 12 states.
- **Watch-item:** the 43–44% AUM growth is therefore to be delivered from a **flat-to-shrinking branch base** plus partnerships. If partnership channels slip, there is no distribution buffer to fall back on.
- **Tech deployment is the real "commissioning" line:** Moneyboxx One LOS and Sikka app are launched but benefit is deferred — *"real benefit will come in coming months."*
capital allocation:
- **Capital position:** CAR 29.48%, described as *"comfortable… providing sufficient headroom to support future growth."*
- **Equity:** *"Right now, for the current plan, our net worth is adequate… for the current plan of FY '27, equity is not inadequate, but we'll keep looking for it."* Then, more concretely: *"The history tells us that in the last 7 years, every single year we have raised some amount of equity. So I think this year will not be any exception, but let's see… definitely, on our side, we will target to raise some equity in the second half of the year."* **Dilution should be treated as the base case** on management's own 7-for-7 track record, but it is undated beyond "second half" and explicitly market-conditional: *"market scenario needs to improve because of this war and all."*
- **Liabilities:** *"we continue to see strong support from our lending partners. Our relationships with banks, NBFCs, capital market participants and development-focused institutions continue to deepen."* No cost-of-funds number, no lender count, no borrowing-mix disclosure was given on this call — a gap versus peer disclosure.
- **Co-lending** is being explored in secured to grow AUM without consuming own capital.
- **Recovery capital:** the ARC transaction plus Section 138 and SARFAESI action are the stated route for legacy stress — *"from May onwards, we have started taking SARFAESI action in these cases also."*
risks & watch-items:
1. **The ARC transaction is un-quantified** — size, consideration and accounting were not disclosed, yet it explains both the AUM decline and part of the NPA improvement. This is the single biggest disclosure gap on the call.
2. **Guidance credibility gap:** 43–44% AUM growth from a **shrinking branch base**, a discontinued sub-₹5-lakh secured product, and a run-off unsecured book — after a year management itself calls *"definitely bad."* The growth must come almost entirely from ticket-size uplift and unproven partnership channels.
3. **Credit cost guided to fall from 3.32% to below 2% in one year** while simultaneously growing AUM 43–44% — vintage-seasoning risk. New-book growth typically defers, not eliminates, credit cost.
4. **Structural margin squeeze:** yield down (secured + partnership mix) with opex fix dependent on AUM growth that has not yet materialised. If AUM growth misses, both legs miss together.
5. **Rural cash-flow / monsoon / input-supply risk, flagged by management:** *"If fertilizers supply get impacted or rainfall is short, next year, you can have not so great agriculture productivity, which could then have some impact… the bad scenario could be some food grain inflation, lower productivity in agriculture in the next crop season."*
6. **Sector-level contagion risk already realised once:** *"What initially began in the unsecured and MFI ecosystem gradually impacted parts of secured lending markets as well, particularly lenders operating in a small ticket size, self-employed and micro enterprise financing… last 2 years, especially in portfolio, the customer overlap with MFI borrowers was higher."*
7. **Sector-specific input shocks reach the borrower directly** — *"because of this LPG shortage, we stopped lending to restaurants"* — an entire borrower vertical was switched off. Demonstrates how narrow the underwriting margin of safety is.
8. **Attrition history:** *"the vast attrition came"* over the last two years alongside *"a very significant change in our team, whether at a state head level."* The new leadership team is unproven together.
9. **Equity-raise overhang** in H2 FY27 (dilution) against management's own *"market scenario needs to improve because of this war and all."*
10. **Profitability is de-minimis** — ₹1.34cr FY26 PAT gives essentially no earnings buffer against any adverse provisioning surprise.
11. **Digital lending is unsecured** — a new unsecured product launched into the same environment that caused the damage, albeit explicitly small.
12. **Disclosure gaps on this call:** no cost of funds, no lender count, no borrowing mix, no ROA/ROE, no absolute disbursement figure for Q4/FY26, no branch count, no employee count, no Stage-3 PCR.
management quality / tone: Unusually candid and non-defensive — a notable positive on an otherwise weak set of numbers. Management repeatedly conceded points rather than deflecting: *"Rushbh I don't disagree with you. Our cost is high"*; *"last year has been definitely bad, and things were not right"*; *"I don't disagree that yield will decrease"*; *"one of the lacking points was a growth in AUM."* The co-founder also volunteered a falsifiable credibility test — *"generally, historically, we have tried to ensure that the number we give to our lenders is achieved"* — and gave a specific monthly checkpoint (*"you will see in next 3, 4 months, the numbers will be better than the Q4"*). Against that: the AUM sentence was internally contradictory ("6% growth" vs "the decline"), the ARC transaction was mentioned twice but never sized, several partnership counterparties were left unnamed (*"one of the very large unit"*), and the call ran short with only three questioners (two of them from the sell-side/individual retail) — thin analyst engagement. Closing remarks were perfunctory. Tone: honest operator mid-repair, not a promoter selling a story.
non-obvious takeaways:
1. **Solar lending is being used as a seasonality hedge, not just a growth product.** This is the sharpest strategic insight on the call and is easy to miss: *"we also realized for a very long time that April, May, June becomes weaker because of the kind of portfolio we have been building. And this February, March or April, May, June is one of the strongest for solar… But these solar loans are at peak in April, May, June. So that's what we have started. So next year, you will see that this low phase of April, May, June will be handled through solar loans."* The company is deliberately counter-cycling its own disbursement calendar.
2. **Solar loans are classified as SECURED** — via hypothecation of the solar asset — **and additionally carry a second-loss guarantee**. So the product simultaneously improves the secured-mix ratio (toward the 80% Mar-27 target), carries ~22.5–24% yield (i.e. **near-unsecured yield economics**), and incurs **no sales cost**. That combination is the single best unit-economic item in the whole call, and it is the mechanism by which management reconciles "yield will decrease" with "credit cost below 2%".
3. **The FLDG/second-loss structures are being negotiated BEFORE product launch, as policy** — a genuine change in institutional behaviour: *"last 12 months was the first time we were looking for FLDG program, second loss fees guarantee program, before starting anything. So that already incorporates the feeling that be cautious on whatever we do."*
4. **"Moving up the chain" is an industry-wide crowding trade, and management says so.** *"every lender is trying to move up the chain, MFI moving up to secured, or maybe lending for players like us who are doing like INR3 lakh, INR5 lakhs, 6 lakhs are also moving to the more, I mean, better houses, better collateral, better customers."* The implication management does not draw: the ₹6–9 lakh secured segment Moneyboxx is migrating INTO is receiving simultaneous inflows from MFIs moving up and from banks/HFCs moving down — competitive intensity and yield compression there are likely to be worse than the guidance assumes.
5. **The demand story is a lender-supply story.** *"it's not that appetite is not there or the demand is not there. But I think from the lenders' perspective… everyone has tightened the norms of lending."* The AUM shrinkage is self-inflicted underwriting choice, not absent demand — which is why management believes it is reversible on command.
6. **Bucket resolution rates roughly doubled** (30–35% → >70% / >75%) — a bigger operational swing than the headline GNPA move and, unlike GNPA, **not** confounded by the ARC transfer. This is arguably the cleanest evidence of genuine collection-machinery improvement on the call.
7. **The "first 5.5 years including COVID had no collection stress"** framing — *"If I talk about in our last 7 years of operation, first 5.5 years and that is why I'm saying, including COVID, there has never been a collection stress… So in the last 1.5 years, collection has become a task."* Management is arguing the last 18 months are the anomaly, not the norm. That is a testable claim, and the whole FY27 case rests on it.
8. **A borrower vertical was switched off entirely on an input shock** (restaurants, on LPG shortage) — evidence of a genuinely active, sector-level underwriting overlay, but also of how thin the buffer is.
9. **Green shoots cited are second-hand, not own-book:** *"we are hearing comments from MFI industry also that last quarter has been good, and there are green shoots. I mean, the leverage is really low now in the MFI segment."* Treat as sector colour, not company evidence.

3. **The FLDG/second-loss structures are being negotiated BEFORE product launch, as policy** — a genuine change in institutional behaviour: *"last 12 months was the first time we were looking for FLDG program, second loss fees guarantee program, before starting anything. hero.oneLiner: FY26 was an explicitly self-described year of "transition, correction and strengthening" — Moneyboxx sacrificed growth to fix a book that got caught in the MFI-guardrail spillover, and the asset-quality repair is now visible and large: GNPA 6.61% → 3.59%, NNPA 3.42% → 1.75%, bucket-1/bucket-2 resolution rates at "the highest level achieved by the company since inception". The cost of that repair is that the P&L is barely above breakeven (FY26 PAT ₹1.34cr on ₹232cr total income) because opex (12.8%) is carried against a shrunken ₹893cr AUM. The FY27 thesis is entirely an operating-leverage bet: management has told its lenders a **43–44% AUM jump** and expects credit cost **below 2%**, to be delivered through a secured mix pivot (68% → target ~80% by Mar-27), FLDG/second-loss-backed partnership sourcing that carries no sales cost, and a new solar/renewable-asset product targeted at ~10% of AUM.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Tagline "Empowering MSMEs in Semi-urban & Rural India"; mission is "To deliver easy, cost-efficient and technology driven financing solutions to aspiring microentrepreneurs" and vision to be "The Lender of Choice" for deserving microentrepreneurs in India.
- Described as a "National franchise with presence in 12 States" with a "Proven scalability and 'phygital' branch model"; "Gained national presence in 7 years with presence in 12 states (Jun'26)".
- Strategic pivot stated as "Focus on upper tier of Small & Micro enterprise segment" - target customer is secured business loans with ATS Rs 10 Lakhs and a strong credit profile (650+ bureau score).
- Impact positioning: 100% PSL qualified, ~50% Women (AUM), 19% New-to-credit (AUM), 232k+ borrowers funded, and a stated aim of "Enabling 2x growth in disposable income of borrowers in 3 years".
- AUM by customer segment (Jun'26): Livestock 49.3%, Retail Traders 20.3%, Service 12.8%, Kirana 8.5%, Manufacturing 8.3%, Solar 0.8%.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
No subsidiaries were discussed — this is a standalone NBFC. Segment detail is by product:
- **Secured MSME business loans (core, ~68% of AUM incl. 5% guarantee-backed unsecured):** ATS ₹6 lakh, run-rate ticket ₹8–9 lakh. **In April the company discontinued sub-₹5-lakh secured tickets for most branches** — *"in April, we discontinued below INR5 lakh ticket size in secured for most of the branches."*
- **Unsecured micro-enterprise loans (run-off):** *"on a branch level, there is only one state which is allowed to do unsecured loan."*
- **Renewable-energy / solar-asset loans (new in FY26):** financing the **replacement of diesel engines** in *"solar atta chakki, oil expellers, jaggery units, telecom towers."* Customer profile: operators with agri land plus a machine business (atta chakki, oil expeller, RO water plant, sheet-metal fabrication). **ATS ~₹4 lakh; tenure ~4 years; interest rate ~22%, overall yield 22.5% rising to ~23–24% including all fees.** Classified as **secured** — *"there is a hypothecation of solar assets against these loans"* — and carries a second-loss guarantee after 3% loss. Critically, *"we are not incurring sales cost here. So these are direct leads which are coming through partners."*
- **Digital lending (launching Q1FY27):** *"This is the quarter we are wanting to start it. It will be a small piece… this will be unsecured lending, just to mention. We will start small here but slowly increase it."* Enabled by the newly released in-house LOS.
- **Credit-protection overlays:** Rabo Foundation — **3.3% first-loss default guarantee**. Shell Foundation — **10% second-loss guarantee after initial 3% loss coverage**, for loans financing green assets.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
Not applicable in the conventional sense (lending business). Pipeline visibility on this call came from three channel signals rather than a book:
- **Solar/renewable ramp (stated monthly progression):** *"in April, we started renewable energy loans and the expansion was around INR50 lakhs, which is 10x in May, and the number could reach about INR5 crores in May."*
- **OEM partnership pipeline:** *"we have been doing OEM partnerships directly. Solar is one example. We are directly dealing with the OEMs to generate business. And in June, another 2 partnerships are starting."*
- **Cattle-loan partnership:** *"on the cattle loan side also, we are joining a partnership with one of the very large unit where we will fund some loans based on the FLDG programs."* Counterparty not named, size not disclosed.
- Management repeatedly asserts a monthly-improving disbursement trajectory from May-2026 onward — *"from this month onwards that it's only up and up in terms of disbursement number on a monthly basis."*

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **AUM growth (FY27):** *"for all the lenders, we have projected about 43% to 44% AUM jump for this year… This is what we are giving to all our lenders. And generally, historically, we have tried to ensure that the number we give to our lenders is achieved."* — Note this is framed as the number **submitted to lenders**, not a formal investor guidance; management volunteered the historical hit-rate as the credibility anchor.
- **Credit cost (FY27):** *"This year, we seriously expect that this number should go down below 2%"* (from 3.32% in FY26).
- **Secured mix:** *"targeting nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027, including loans backed by guarantee program"* (from ~68% now).
- **Renewable/solar product:** *"maybe around 10% of the AUM by March '27"*; separately *"I think this business will be about 10% of AUM this year."*
- **Partnership channel:** *"there is a planning where we are trying to do 20%, 25% of the monthly business through direct partnership, which does not involve sales team."*
- **Near-term disbursement trajectory:** *"you will see in next 3, 4 months, the numbers will be better than the Q4, which has gone by"*; *"the second quarter in terms of disbursement should be far better than last year."*
- **Yield direction (explicit negative guide):** *"I don't disagree that yield will decrease because of the secured lending or even on the partnership business side."*
- **Equity:** *"for the current plan of FY '27, equity is not inadequate, but we'll keep looking for it… we will target to raise some equity in the second half of the year."*
- **Branch/geography (explicit negative guide):** no new states in FY27; branch network *"only coming down"* — see §8.
- **NOT guided:** no ROA/ROE target, no absolute AUM/PAT number, no NIM target, no opex-ratio target. Management deflected the ROA/ROE question into a qualitative opex-and-credit-cost answer.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
1. **Partnership/OEM-sourced lending with embedded credit protection** — the structural bet of the year. It attacks both cost lines at once: no sales team (opex) and FLDG/second-loss cover (credit cost). Targeted at 20–25% of monthly business.
2. **MSME solarization** — management frames this as demand-pull, not product-push: *"diesel prices have increased and more and more people want to switch to solar power for running atta chakki, oil expellers."* It also doubles as a **seasonality hedge** (see §12).
3. **Branch vintage maturation** — *"Many of our branches are still in early vintage state, particularly within the first 24 months of operation. As these branches mature, productivity continues to improve steadily, and this embedded growth opportunity is expected to support operating leverage and business growth over the coming years without requiring aggressive branch expansion."*
4. **Co-lending in the secured space** — *"We will look for some co-lending partners in the secured space."* Early-stage intent only.
5. **Digital lending** — optionality, explicitly small at launch.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **The central tension of the story: yield is guided down while opex must come down faster.** Management concedes the yield give-up outright — *"I don't disagree that yield will decrease because of the secured lending or even on the partnership business side"* — and pins the offset on cost: *"But what we are trying to do here is that we have to reduce our opex."*
- **Opex is a denominator problem, not a wage problem** — management's explicit diagnosis: *"Our cost is high. So one of the biggest reasons is that our AUM is low… as AUM grows, the cost will keep coming down… what we have to really work hard on is to improve the AUM, so that the opex automatically starts declining."* And: *"I will not say that as a company we are overpaying or we are bringing staff at a much higher scale. So that is not true. I mean, our costing is aligned with the market."*
- ⚠️ The analyst's framing — *"our employee cost as a percentage of total assets under management also appears on the higher side, basically, if I'm not wrong, it's around 37%, 38%. I don't have the number in front of me right away"* — was **explicitly caveated by the analyst himself** and **never confirmed numerically by management**. Do not propagate it as a company figure.
- **Three-lever cost plan:** (a) partnership sourcing removes sales cost; (b) FLDG/second-loss programs cap credit cost; (c) decentralized credit underwriting cuts turnaround time — *"the deployment of a decentralized credit underwriting model is helping reduce turnaround time and enhance operating efficiency."*
- **Management's own benchmark for what "solved" looks like:** *"even players who work at 15% or 12%, they make money. So it's a lot about getting your credit cost, opex and collection costs under control."*
- FY26 stated levels: **NIM 13.9%, opex 12.8%, credit cost 3.32%** — i.e. on management's own stated numbers the three lines very nearly consume each other, which is consistent with the ₹1.34cr PAT.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Capital position:** CAR 29.48%, described as *"comfortable… providing sufficient headroom to support future growth."*
- **Equity:** *"Right now, for the current plan, our net worth is adequate… for the current plan of FY '27, equity is not inadequate, but we'll keep looking for it."* Then, more concretely: *"The history tells us that in the last 7 years, every single year we have raised some amount of equity. So I think this year will not be any exception, but let's see… definitely, on our side, we will target to raise some equity in the second half of the year."* **Dilution should be treated as the base case** on management's own 7-for-7 track record, but it is undated beyond "second half" and explicitly market-conditional: *"market scenario needs to improve because of this war and all."*
- **Liabilities:** *"we continue to see strong support from our lending partners. Our relationships with banks, NBFCs, capital market participants and development-focused institutions continue to deepen."* No cost-of-funds number, no lender count, no borrowing-mix disclosure was given on this call — a gap versus peer disclosure.
- **Co-lending** is being explored in secured to grow AUM without consuming own capital.
- **Recovery capital:** the ARC transaction plus Section 138 and SARFAESI action are the stated route for legacy stress — *"from May onwards, we have started taking SARFAESI action in these cases also."*

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Unusually candid and non-defensive — a notable positive on an otherwise weak set of numbers. Management repeatedly conceded points rather than deflecting: *"Rushbh I don't disagree with you. Our cost is high"*; *"last year has been definitely bad, and things were not right"*; *"I don't disagree that yield will decrease"*; *"one of the lacking points was a growth in AUM."* The co-founder also volunteered a falsifiable credibility test — *"generally, historically, we have tried to ensure that the number we give to our lenders is achieved"* — and gave a specific monthly checkpoint (*"you will see in next 3, 4 months, the numbers will be better than the Q4"*). Against that: the AUM sentence was internally contradictory ("6% growth" vs "the decline"), the ARC transaction was mentioned twice but never sized, several partnership counterparties were left unnamed (*"one of the very large unit"*), and the call ran short with only three questioners (two of them from the sell-side/individual retail) — thin analyst engagement. Closing remarks were perfunctory. Tone: honest operator mid-repair, not a promoter selling a story.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
Management evidenced three durable advantages on this call (each with its supporting quote/number):
- **Impact-capital relationships that convert into hard credit enhancement.** The Rabo Foundation **3.3% FLDG** and Shell Foundation **10% second-loss guarantee after initial 3% loss coverage** are not soft ESG affiliations — they are balance-sheet loss absorbers that competitors of this size generally do not carry. Sourced via the Cattle AI platform and para-vet services: *"Different initiatives such as our Cattle AI platform and complementary Para-vet services are also helping us build strong global partnerships with institutions such as Rabo Foundation, Gates Foundation, Water.org, Shell Foundation and Accion."*
- **Proprietary underwriting/collection tech stack for a segment that is normally paper-based** — in-house LOS "Moneyboxx One", the Sikka app, ML/AI-enabled **Cattle AI** underwriting, and **MB Collect** digital collections: *"helping improve underwriting quality, strengthen fraud checks and maintain strong credit discipline."*
- **Senior talent density well above the book's size** — *"my state heads who are managing about INR100 crores here have been managing almost INR2,000 crores from where they have come in… we have taken the best of profiles from the best of the companies who have like 15 to 20 years kind of experience in building this kind of book."* Note this is presented as a **moat and a cost problem simultaneously** — it is the direct cause of the opex overhang in §7.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **The ARC transaction is un-quantified** — size, consideration and accounting were not disclosed, yet it explains both the AUM decline and part of the NPA improvement. This is the single biggest disclosure gap on the call.
2. **Guidance credibility gap:** 43–44% AUM growth from a **shrinking branch base**, a discontinued sub-₹5-lakh secured product, and a run-off unsecured book — after a year management itself calls *"definitely bad."* The growth must come almost entirely from ticket-size uplift and unproven partnership channels.
3. **Credit cost guided to fall from 3.32% to below 2% in one year** while simultaneously growing AUM 43–44% — vintage-seasoning risk. New-book growth typically defers, not eliminates, credit cost.
4. **Structural margin squeeze:** yield down (secured + partnership mix) with opex fix dependent on AUM growth that has not yet materialised. If AUM growth misses, both legs miss together.
5. **Rural cash-flow / monsoon / input-supply risk, flagged by management:** *"If fertilizers supply get impacted or rainfall is short, next year, you can have not so great agriculture productivity, which could then have some impact… the bad scenario could be some food grain inflation, lower productivity in agriculture in the next crop season."*
6. **Sector-level contagion risk already realised once:** *"What initially began in the unsecured and MFI ecosystem gradually impacted parts of secured lending markets as well, particularly lenders operating in a small ticket size, self-employed and micro enterprise financing… last 2 years, especially in portfolio, the customer overlap with MFI borrowers was higher."*
7. **Sector-specific input shocks reach the borrower directly** — *"because of this LPG shortage, we stopped lending to restaurants"* — an entire borrower vertical was switched off. Demonstrates how narrow the underwriting margin of safety is.
8. **Attrition history:** *"the vast attrition came"* over the last two years alongside *"a very significant change in our team, whether at a state head level."* The new leadership team is unproven together.
9. **Equity-raise overhang** in H2 FY27 (dilution) against management's own *"market scenario needs to improve because of this war and all."*
10. **Profitability is de-minimis** — ₹1.34cr FY26 PAT gives essentially no earnings buffer against any adverse provisioning surprise.
11. **Digital lending is unsecured** — a new unsecured product launched into the same environment that caused the damage, albeit explicitly small.
12. **Disclosure gaps on this call:** no cost of funds, no lender count, no borrowing mix, no ROA/ROE, no absolute disbursement figure for Q4/FY26, no branch count, no employee count, no Stage-3 PCR.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
1. **Solar lending is being used as a seasonality hedge, not just a growth product.** This is the sharpest strategic insight on the call and is easy to miss: *"we also realized for a very long time that April, May, June becomes weaker because of the kind of portfolio we have been building. And this February, March or April, May, June is one of the strongest for solar… But these solar loans are at peak in April, May, June. So that's what we have started. So next year, you will see that this low phase of April, May, June will be handled through solar loans."* The company is deliberately counter-cycling its own disbursement calendar.
2. **Solar loans are classified as SECURED** — via hypothecation of the solar asset — **and additionally carry a second-loss guarantee**. So the product simultaneously improves the secured-mix ratio (toward the 80% Mar-27 target), carries ~22.5–24% yield (i.e. **near-unsecured yield economics**), and incurs **no sales cost**. That combination is the single best unit-economic item in the whole call, and it is the mechanism by which management reconciles "yield will decrease" with "credit cost below 2%".
3. **The FLDG/second-loss structures are being negotiated BEFORE product launch, as policy** — a genuine change in institutional behaviour: *"last 12 months was the first time we were looking for FLDG program, second loss fees guarantee program, before starting anything. So that already incorporates the feeling that be cautious on whatever we do."*
4. **"Moving up the chain" is an industry-wide crowding trade, and management says so.** *"every lender is trying to move up the chain, MFI moving up to secured, or maybe lending for players like us who are doing like INR3 lakh, INR5 lakhs, 6 lakhs are also moving to the more, I mean, better houses, better collateral, better customers."* The implication management does not draw: the ₹6–9 lakh secured segment Moneyboxx is migrating INTO is receiving simultaneous inflows from MFIs moving up and from banks/HFCs moving down — competitive intensity and yield compression there are likely to be worse than the guidance assumes.
5. **The demand story is a lender-supply story.** *"it's not that appetite is not there or the demand is not there. But I think from the lenders' perspective… everyone has tightened the norms of lending."* The AUM shrinkage is self-inflicted underwriting choice, not absent demand — which is why management believes it is reversible on command.
6. **Bucket resolution rates roughly doubled** (30–35% → >70% / >75%) — a bigger operational swing than the headline GNPA move and, unlike GNPA, **not** confounded by the ARC transfer. This is arguably the cleanest evidence of genuine collection-machinery improvement on the call.
7. **The "first 5.5 years including COVID had no collection stress"** framing — *"If I talk about in our last 7 years of operation, first 5.5 years and that is why I'm saying, including COVID, there has never been a collection stress… So in the last 1.5 years, collection has become a task."* Management is arguing the last 18 months are the anomaly, not the norm. That is a testable claim, and the whole FY27 case rests on it.
8. **A borrower vertical was switched off entirely on an input shock** (restaurants, on LPG shortage) — evidence of a genuinely active, sector-level underwriting overlay, but also of how thin the buffer is.
9. **Green shoots cited are second-hand, not own-book:** *"we are hearing comments from MFI industry also that last quarter has been good, and there are green shoots. I mean, the leverage is really low now in the MFI segment."* Treat as sector colour, not company evidence.

qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this, FIRST note for this company):** Baseline established. FY26 = self-described *"year of transition, correction and strengthening."* AUM ₹893cr (declined YoY on an un-quantified ARC transaction); GNPA 6.61% → 3.59%, NNPA 3.42% → 1.75%; credit cost 3.32% (FY25 3.43%); NIM 13.9%; opex 12.8%; FY26 PAT ₹1.34cr (FY25 ₹1.25cr); CAR 29.48%. Secured mix 45% → 68% of AUM; secured disbursement 49% → 67%. Sub-₹5-lakh secured tickets discontinued at most branches in April-2026; unsecured lending now permitted in one state only. Solar/renewable-asset lending launched (secured via hypothecation, ~22.5–24% yield, ATS ₹4 lakh, 4-year tenure, no sales cost). SARFAESI action commenced May-2026. Branch network consolidating; no new states in FY27. **Guidance to verify:** AUM +43–44% FY27 · credit cost <2% · secured mix ~80% by Mar-27 · solar ~10% of AUM by Mar-27 · partnerships 20–25% of monthly business · equity raise in H2 FY27.
- _Q1 FY27 → check:_ (1) did the **43–44% AUM growth** trajectory start — management promised *"in next 3, 4 months, the numbers will be better than the Q4"* and *"the second quarter in terms of disbursement should be far better than last year"*; (2) **did the 2 June-2026 OEM partnerships actually start** (see trigger below), and what share of monthly business is partnership-sourced vs the 20–25% target; (3) **credit-cost trajectory toward <2%** — and whether new-book seasoning defers it; (4) **is the ARC transaction finally sized** (consideration, pool, security receipts) so the organic vs transferred split of the NPA improvement can be separated; (5) **solar book size** vs the ~10%-of-AUM path and whether the April–June seasonality hedge worked; (6) digital-lending launch actually happened and stayed small; (7) any **equity raise** progress (H2 FY27 stated intent, 7-for-7 historical base rate); (8) whether disclosure gaps close — cost of funds, lender count, branch count, PCR.

### Near-term trigger (SPEC §10)
- **Trigger:** Two additional direct OEM partnerships commencing in **June 2026** — the delivery mechanism for the partnership channel targeted at 20–25% of monthly business, which is in turn the main engine behind the 43–44% FY27 AUM guidance for a company whose branch network is shrinking.
- **Verbatim:** *"Plus, we have been doing OEM partnerships directly. Solar is one example. We are directly dealing with the OEMs to generate business. And in June, another 2 partnerships are starting."*
- **Type / impact / date:** Product-launch · **Medium** (vs own size: the channel is targeted at 20–25% of monthly business for a ₹893cr-AUM lender, i.e. comfortably above the ≳15% materiality bar, and it is the only distribution growth lever given the branch base is contracting) · **June 2026**.
- ⚠️ **THE TRIGGER WINDOW HAS ALREADY LAPSED.** The call was held **29-May-2026**, so the SPEC §10 "next ~3 months" window is ~**Jun–Aug 2026**. As of today (**13-Aug-2026**) that window is effectively closed — the June start date is ~2.5 months past. This should be treated as a **verification item for the Q1 FY27 note (did the two partnerships actually start, and what did they contribute?)**, not as a forward-looking catalyst. Recommend it is **excluded from `triggers.csv`** on freshness grounds unless the owner wants lapsed triggers retained for guidance-hit/miss scoring.
- **Rejected candidates (for audit trail):** (a) *digital lending launch* — hard-dated to the quarter (*"This is the quarter we are wanting to start it"*) but **management itself sized it as immaterial** (*"It will be a small piece… We will start small here"*) → fails the impact test; (b) *solar at ~10% of AUM* and *~80% secured mix* — both dated **March 2027**, i.e. FY27-end → outside the ~3-month window; (c) *equity raise* — *"second half of the year"*, undated and market-conditional → fails the hard-date test; (d) *the ₹5cr May solar run-rate* — refers to May-2026, already elapsed at the call date.
